summary: The new consent, personal-block and user-report flows have strict ownership, bounded fields, server timestamps and admin-only review. Emulator tests cover atomic block/report writes, private reads, spoofed targets, self-unban, consent spoofing and publication bypasses. This is a scoped moderation review, not a certification of every legacy collection.

findings.issue: Existing properties and comment reads are public at database level; public app views apply publication/moderation filtering. Private reports and block lists are protected independently.
findings.recommendation: A separate migration can tighten legacy query/read contracts without breaking existing clients.

findings.issue: Unrelated legacy analytics, followers and notifications retain broad create/update contracts and incomplete field limits.
findings.recommendation: Audit and migrate these collections separately with their existing clients and server functions.

verified_attacks: comment hiding bypass through recursive match
impersonating a verified office for direct publication
